**My thinking, as this farmer:**

I've been working this land my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn, and so did I. Here in Quzhou, the soil is deep loam, the groundwater is reachable, and the county agricultural station keeps pushing us toward the same rotation they've always recommended — winter wheat, then summer maize on the same plots. That's what my neighbors do. That's what makes sense.

I have about 10 mu of contracted land. All of it will go into wheat-maize double cropping. I won't try cotton — prices have been bad and I don't have the labor. My wife and I can manage the wheat and corn ourselves, maybe hire day labor at harvest.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved seed from the township seed shop — the same variety my neighbor used last year, gave him 450 kg per mu. I'll do four waterings: one before sowing to wet the bed, the winter freeze water in December, jointing water in April, and grain-fill water in May. I always do four. My father did four.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at jointing. I know the station says I use too much nitrogen, but I'd rather not risk a thin harvest. I'll spray herbicide once in spring, and watch for aphids and rust — spray if I see them.

After wheat comes off in June, I'll rotary-till and get the maize in quick. Summer rain usually helps. One irrigation at the start if it's dry, maybe another at grain fill. Herbicide once. Maize basically takes care of itself compared to wheat.
